mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS), or the rate remains below 5.25% for the subsequent 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns within the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same or
failure_condition: The correlation between PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline is not statistically significant (p > 0.05), or SPX 20-day returns show no positive deviation from a baseline model using only lagged SPX and macro variables.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating supply-side demand, which anticipates a rebound in consumer and business activity and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month growth > 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: INDPRO growth remains below 2% for the subsequent 5-day window, or SPX 5-day returns are negative despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month while the prior month's increase was below 0.1%, it indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain higher rates and suppressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month increase > 0.3% following a prior month's increase < 0.1%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from a period with stable inflation (p > 0.05 in t-test), or CPIAUCSL shows no such surprise pattern in the walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining residential mortgage applications (implied by HOUST) suggest tightening credit conditions, which reduces risk appetite and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: HOUST does not decline for two consecutive months, or SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% followed by a sustained rise in labor participation (PAYEMS) above 7.5% for the next month indicates a labor market transition that boosts equity valuations and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% and PAYEMS rises above 7.5% in the following month
failure_condition: The UNRATE-PAYEMS interaction is not predictive of SPX returns (p > 0.05 in logistic regression), or the direction of returns is opposite to the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (implied by GDPC1) grow by more than 4% in a single month, it reflects strong consumer demand that is not yet fully priced into equities, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth does not exceed 4% in the subsequent 5-day window, or SPX 5-day returns are not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of falling industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months suggests a supply-side contraction, which typically precedes a market correction and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers in the following 20-day window, or SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
